concept: Turn a school hallway into a museum: choose kid artworks for a theme and say why, give each the right frame, stand or case and hang it at kid height, then play curator, guard, guide and visitor on opening day.

title: Traveling Art Show
subject: arts
concept: Get six student artworks ready for a month at the town library: choose them with a theme checklist, protect and place each away from sun, heat and busy hands, write labels, then fast-forward a month to see what survived.

title: Place Mood Makeover
subject: arts
concept: Give an ordinary place (a bus stop, the lunchroom, a porch) a mood by changing its light, colors, weather and details, tag your clues, and revise until the Mood Reader finds every clue pointing the same way.

title: School Wall Mural
subject: arts
concept: Plan a mural for the school's street-facing wall: gather what neighbors care about, judge four sketches against your criteria, test the winner from the sidewalk, a bus window and five summers of sun, and argue for it at the board meeting.

title: Sketchbook Process Journal
subject: arts
concept: Start from a present-day issue and an older art tradition, log each step from thumbnail to plan in a sketchbook, and watch an idea map show where research and history changed your idea and where your own voice broke from the tradition.

title: Parade and Bedtime Music
subject: arts
concept: Sort short original tunes into the moments they fit (bedtime, a parade, a birthday, a rainy day) and name the clue; then turn one tune's speed and loudness until a parade march becomes a lullaby.

title: Name Song Practice
subject: arts
concept: Clap your name and pick a favorite thing to make a short sol-mi song, sing it, hear yourself back, pick one fix and sing it again, then perform the better take with feeling for a stuffed-animal audience.

title: Recorder Concert Rehearsal
subject: arts
concept: Lead a recorder group's rehearsal: mark each take on a checklist, find who and which bar went wrong, give one note and hear the next take fix just that, then join the spring concert yourself.

title: Cartoon Soundtrack Mixer
subject: arts
concept: Score a silent cartoon on a timeline (music cues, sound effects, tempo, loudness, instruments), then press Mood Swap and see the same pictures turn funny, scary or sad under a different score.

title: Folk Song Arranger
subject: arts
concept: Arrange a public-domain folk tune for a small band and a named occasion: pick instruments, add an intro and a new section, run the arranger's checks for range and balance, revise and explain each change.

title: Cover Version Review
subject: arts
concept: Two performers sing the same public-domain song very differently; line them up on a difference strip, mark what each changed (tempo, loudness, instruments), and write a review where every claim points at a moment you can play.

title: Recital Practice Plan
subject: arts
concept: Plan a ten-minute recital four weeks out: choose a set for the venue and audience, budget practice on the hardest passages, judge takes on a rubric you build, and write why the set matters to you.

title: Puppet Show Feelings
subject: arts
concept: Watch a sock-puppet show, then go backstage and change one thing at a time (head tilt, voice speed, bounce) to see the audience read a new feeling; pick the ending you like and say how a puppet is like you.

title: Moon Base Drama
subject: arts
concept: Join Commander Ada's moon base crew: pick a prop that shows your job, answer her in role, use true moon facts to save the greenhouse before the long night, then rewind and change one line to see the story change.

title: Neighborhood Issue Play
subject: arts
concept: Hear neighbors talk about a real kind of problem (a closed park, a missing crosswalk, a new family), turn them into characters who want things, build a paper toy theater with set and costumes, and perform your short play.

title: Audience Talkback
subject: arts
concept: Two versions of one short scene feel different; swap costumes, lights, voices and music between them until you find what made the difference, then judge both with your own criteria and back it with your experience.

title: Three Viewpoints Scene
subject: arts
concept: Devise a short scene about a school issue from three viewpoints: draft its beats, build on a devising partner's ideas, tighten the pacing until the turn lands, then perform one role live with the others voiced.

title: Scene Staging Comparison
subject: arts
concept: Watch two productions of one public-domain scene side by side, record your reactions moment by moment, then compare them with a classmate's and find how culture, era and staging choices made you see it differently.

title: Stage Lighting Plot
subject: arts
concept: Light the last scene of A Doll's House: research the period's lamps and windows, hang and aim instruments, pick color, level and cues, then run the scene and revise until the light turns when the story turns.

title: Monologue Rehearsal
subject: arts
concept: Pick a monologue, answer the given circumstances (where am I, what do I want, what is in my way), try vocal and physical choices in rehearsal, and perform it for a chosen audience while connecting it to your own beliefs.

title: Feeling Scarf Dance
subject: arts
concept: Pick a feeling, build a three-part dance (a starting shape, a moving middle, an ending shape), watch a dancer's scarf show it, then dance it yourself with any soft cloth for an audience at home or in class.

title: Family Dance Night
subject: arts
concept: At family dance night in the school gym, families teach a dance from home: watch the animated dancers, copy a move and describe it with dance words, pick a favorite part, and find out how each dance connects to the people and place it comes from.

title: Poem to Movement
subject: arts
concept: Pick a poem, painting or sound, turn its words and qualities into a movement phrase, draw its floor map, then let a viewer guess the source and revise until the dance carries it.

title: Recital Stage Directions
subject: arts
concept: Place recital dancers on a nine-area stage, flip to the audience to see why stage left is your right, add costumes and lights, read two pieces' main ideas from an audience seat, then dance the stage areas yourself.

title: Dancers on Tour
subject: arts
concept: A six-dancer piece tours a gym, a park and a small theater; scout each space, adapt spacing, timing and focus, apply the choreographer's notes, and keep the dancers safe with the right warm-up for each surface.

title: Dance Hall Decades
subject: arts
concept: Walk through social dance halls across a century, learn one pattern in each, see who made the dance and who was kept out, and judge two dances against your own way of moving.

title: Choreography for a Cause
subject: arts
concept: Research an issue in a fact file, turn its data, quotes and photos into movement motifs, arrange them in a dance structure that carries your point, and revise from viewers' notes until they can say what it is about.

title: Museum Courtyard Performance
subject: arts
concept: Produce a dance concert in a museum courtyard over six weeks: adapt the piece to columns, a fountain, a stone floor and a balcony audience, plan safe rehearsals, spend a budget on light and sound, and lead the crew to opening night.

title: Sound and Picture Book
subject: arts
concept: Plan a three-page story with picture cards, draw or snap a picture and record a sound for each page, play your book, then swap two sounds or pages and hear the story change.

title: Field Trip Slideshow
subject: arts
concept: After a class trip to the aquarium, take each crew job in turn (camera, sound, speaker), get its one skill right, then set up the room and present your slideshow to visiting families.

title: Cereal Ad Questions
subject: arts
concept: Watch a silly made-up cereal ad, pull out its music, pictures and words one at a time until only a plain bowl is left, say what the ad wanted you to think, and find where ads show up in your day.

title: Stop-Motion Clay Shoot
subject: arts
concept: Plan a stop-motion scene on a storyboard, pose clay figures frame by frame, track down why it jumps (a bumped camera, flicker, a hand in the shot, too big a move), fix it, and premiere it.

title: Toy Ad Reality Check
subject: arts
concept: Pause a made-up toy commercial to find the camera tricks, music and words that make the toy look bigger and better, decide what the ad wants you to believe, and rate it against what the toy really does.

title: Morning Show Crew
subject: arts
concept: Run the school morning show for a week with one story: tell it as a video segment, a poster, a site post and an announcement that all say the same thing, then spend crew hours to reach each audience and see who got the message.

title: Viral Video Breakdown
subject: arts
concept: A made-up video of a kid at her grandfather's bakery went viral; take it apart shot by shot, then trace five reposts to find who changed its meaning and dropped her credit, and judge what reposting owes the maker.

title: Mini Documentary Crew
subject: arts
concept: Lead a crew making a five-minute documentary about the last shoe repair shop on Main Street: schedule shoots around real limits, cut interviews, footage and archive photos, test the cut on viewers, and plan the premiere.

title: Weekend Substance Choices
subject: health-pe
concept: Follow a weekend with friends where alcohol, vapes and cannabis edibles show up: choose what to say and do, see how each choice affects the body, the law and friendships, and practice getting help for a friend in trouble.

title: Recess Upstander
subject: health-pe
concept: Watch one recess across a school week: a shove on Monday is a conflict, but teasing the same kid every day is bullying; pick an upstander move each day (say stop, walk them away, tell the aide) and see the other bystanders follow.

title: Worry Size Sorter
subject: health-pe
concept: Sort everyday worries into small, medium and big, try a coping tool for each, find out that big worries go to a trusted adult, and set a one-week coping goal to check off each day.

title: Safety Sweep House
subject: health-pe
concept: Search a house room by room for hazards: medicine within reach, mixed cleaners, a blocked smoke alarm, a stranger asking for an address in a game chat; choose the safe action for each and see what could happen otherwise.

title: Fridge Goal Chart
subject: health-pe
concept: Pick one health goal, like more water or an earlier bedtime, put it on the fridge chart, see what helps and what gets in the way (a TV ad, a busy night), name who can help, and add a star each day.

title: Parachute Teamwork
subject: health-pe
concept: Hold an edge of a rainbow parachute with a circle of kids and play waves, the mushroom and trading places; the parachute flies only when everyone follows the call and takes turns, and a heart check shows how moving feels.

title: Scarf Juggling Ladder
subject: health-pe
concept: Learn scarf juggling one rung at a time, from one scarf to two to three; check each rung against cue cards, log practice tries, and find out that steady practice beats giving up after a drop.

title: Partner Skill Coach
subject: health-pe
concept: Watch slow-motion clips of a player throwing, kicking or shooting, check them against cue cards to find the missed cue, then give one kind, specific tip and see the next try change; partner mode is for real pairs.

title: Friend Moves Practice
subject: sel
concept: Practice friend moves with classroom characters: ask to join a game, share the blocks, take turns, and fix a small problem with a sorry; the class sees how each move changes the friend's face.

title: First Impressions Check
subject: sel
concept: Meet strangers on a city bus, make a snap guess about each one, then reveal more of their story; notice which guesses came from your own biases and how a new perspective changes the picture.

title: Hundred Hop
subject: math
concept: A frog hops along a giant 1-100 path on the projector; the class counts aloud by ones or tens and calls out where it lands before the teacher reveals.

title: Sheep Count
subject: math
concept: Tap each sheep once as it trots into the pen; the last number you say is how many. Count lines, circles and scattered flocks to 20, count out a flock, then the barn door closes: still 8 inside?

title: Snack Scale
subject: math
concept: Pile identical crackers on each side of a seesaw, guess which side has more, then let go. Match them in pairs to see the extras, and compare numeral cards up to 10 the same way.

title: Bus Stop
subject: math
concept: Drive the school bus: riders get on and off at each stop, and you show it with counters and a number sentence. Seat 7 riders every possible way, and count the empty seats to 10.

title: Ten Frame Spillover
subject: math
concept: Drop ladybugs into a ten frame; when it fills, the extras spill onto a second frame and the screen says "ten and 4 more, fourteen, 10 + 4 = 14." Then split a scattered 17 into a ten and the rest.

title: Who Wins?
subject: math
concept: Two animals face off: who is longer, taller or heavier? Guess, then line them up from the same start or set them on a balance; the croc wins longer, the giraffe wins taller.

title: Toy Box Sort
subject: math
concept: Dump a toy box and sort by color, shape or size; each bin counts its toys and the bins line up by count. Then Robo the robot sorts by a secret rule, and you name it.

title: Shape Spy
subject: math
concept: Spy circles, squares, triangles, cubes and cones hiding in a park, kitchen and street; find them tilted and tiny, say where they are (above the slide), and sort flat from solid.

title: Pattern Block Windows
subject: math
concept: Fill stained-glass window outlines with pattern blocks (two triangles make a rhombus), build new window shapes from sticks and clay-ball corners, and count sides and corners to compare shapes.

title: Story Replay
subject: math
concept: Short cartoon stories (birds on a wire, apples in a basket) stop at the question; act them out with counters, pick a number sentence, and the cartoon replays the way your sentence says. All story types within 20.

title: Make Ten Machine
subject: math
concept: Facts roll in on a conveyor as counter trays; use the machine's tools (make ten, flip, double, think addition) to turn a hard fact into an easy one, and see the fact family it belongs to.

title: Balance the Beam
subject: math
concept: A balance scale with numbers on both sides; find the missing weight so it levels. Kills the "equals means the answer comes next" myth.

title: Number Path Rescue
subject: math
concept: Stones on a 1 to 120 river path have washed away; type the missing numbers before the river rises. Start anywhere, cross 100 without writing 1001, and use the chart's patterns to go faster.

title: Crayon Boxes
subject: math
concept: Run the school supply closet: pack loose crayons into boxes of ten, fill table orders as boxes and loose crayons, and on Friday compare two classrooms' stock with >, = and <.

title: Bead Slider
subject: math
concept: Slide beads on a 100-bead string by tens and ones to solve 34 + 20 or 47 + 6, make a new ten when the ones run over, slide back for 10 less or 60 - 30, and write each slide as an equation.

title: Paperclip Ruler
subject: math
concept: Measure classroom objects with paperclips, cubes and shoes; spot Milo's gaps and overlaps, order three things by length, use a string to compare things that can't touch, and see why units must match.

title: Clock Shop
subject: math
concept: Turn the hands of a big geared clock and the digital clock and the sky outside change with it; set clocks for customers to the hour and half hour, and see why the short hand sits between numbers.

title: Class Poll
subject: math
concept: A class votes on pets or snacks one kid at a time; tally the votes, build a picture graph with up to three choices, and answer how many in all and how many more. Run it with your real class too.

title: Pizza Party
subject: math
concept: Cut pizzas and sandwiches so two or four guests get fair shares; uneven cuts get a funny complaint, shares get named (halves, fourths, quarters), and more guests mean smaller pieces.

title: Picky Robot Shapes
subject: math
concept: Compose pictures from flat shapes and from solids (cubes, cones, cylinders), then help a picky robot that accepts only true triangles and squares whatever their color, size or turn, and reuse a shape you built to make a bigger one.

title: Lost and Found
subject: math
concept: Two-step clues about what came in and went out of the lost and found each day ('14 mittens, 6 picked up, 5 more found') point to the box that holds the missing toy.

title: Fact Rally
subject: math
concept: Volley facts back and forth with a tennis bot; strategies (doubles, near doubles, make ten) unlock power shots.

title: Marching Band
subject: math
concept: Line up band members in rows; can everyone have a partner? Arrays reveal odd and even and repeated addition.

title: Place Value Vault
subject: math
concept: Crack three-digit vault codes from clues like "7 tens, 2 hundreds, 0 ones," number names and expanded form; skip-count the dials by 5s, 10s and 100s and compare codes with >, = and <.

title: Jump Line
subject: math
concept: Solve sums and differences to 1000 by drawing your own jumps on an open number line, then compare your path with three classmates' paths to the same answer and explain why each one works.

title: Estimation Station
subject: math
concept: Freight arrives at the station: estimate each item's length, measure it with a ruler, yardstick, meter stick or tape, compare units, and use the ruler as a number line to solve how-much-longer problems.

title: Corner Store
subject: math
concept: Run a snack stand: count coins, make change and close by 3:45 when the bell rings.

title: Lunch Line Data
subject: math
concept: Help the cafeteria plan: turn kids' lunch choices into picture and bar graphs, measure garden carrots to the nearest inch for a line plot, and answer "how many more?" questions from each.

title: Garden Grid
subject: math
concept: Plan a community garden: build beds the gardeners describe (a pentagon, four square corners), split rectangle beds into rows and columns of square plots and count them, and share beds in halves, thirds and fourths.

title: Equal Groups Zoo
subject: math
concept: Feed zoo animals in equal groups; the same feeding shows as a picture, an array, a skip-count and an equation. Share food to divide, flip and split arrays, and see division as a missing factor.

title: Multiplication Dungeon
subject: math
concept: Explore a retro dungeon where every door opens with a multiplication or division fact; a missed fact returns as a sleepy guardian with a strategy hint until the whole times table lights up.

title: Pattern Painter
subject: math
concept: Color the town's multiplication-table mural to make patterns pop (even products, multiples of 5, square numbers); predict the next square and say why the rule always works, then estimate first to check whether a two-step answer can be right.

title: Roller Coaster Rounding
subject: math
concept: A coaster car rolls down to the nearest ten or hundred station (see why 45 rolls up); then run the ride: estimate riders by rounding, add exactly within 1000, and fill trains of 40-seat cars.

title: Fraction Trail
subject: math
concept: Hike a trail from the trailhead (0) to the lake (1), split it into equal legs and place campsites at fractions; find that 1/2 and 2/4 are the same spot, and compare camps on the same trail.

title: Kitchen Lab
subject: math
concept: Cook dinner for 6 p.m.: plan start times on an elapsed-time number line to the minute, weigh ingredients in grams and kilograms, and measure liquids in liters, estimating before you measure.

title: Graph Glow-Up
subject: math
concept: Give crowded graphs a makeover: choose a scale (each picture is 5 votes) so a picture or bar graph fits and still answers "how many more?", and build a line plot from bean pods measured to the quarter inch.

title: Tile the Floor
subject: math
concept: Cover rooms with square tiles until counting gets slow, then shortcut with rows times columns; split L-shaped rooms into rectangles, and split a floor into four equal-area parts for four painters.

title: Fence Builder
subject: math
concept: Build a dog pen with a fixed roll of fencing; every pen uses all of it, but some give the dog more room. Find missing sides, and compare pens with the same fence or the same space.

title: Shape Family Tree
subject: math
concept: Seat quadrilaterals on a family tree where a square sits on two branches; test sides and corners to settle family arguments, and draw a quadrilateral that belongs to none of the named groups.

title: Growth Spurt
subject: math
concept: Two greenhouse plants grow side by side; switch between "taller by" and "times as tall" and watch the gap stay fixed or multiply. Then pack seedlings into trays and decide what the remainder means.

title: Egg Carton Factory
subject: math
concept: Pack egg orders into rectangular cartons with no empty cups; find every carton for 36 eggs (every factor pair), test whether 72 fits cartons of 6, and see that a prime order only fits one long row.

title: Rule Machine
subject: math
concept: Set a start number and a rule, then predict what the machine's pattern will do (all odd? will 100 appear?) before it prints; explain the features the rule never mentions, and crack Cog's mystery tapes.

title: Stadium Count
subject: math
concept: Zoom from one seat to a row, a section, a stadium and a city, ten times more people each step; read crowds in numerals, words and expanded form, compare real stadiums and round for the headline.

title: Area Model Builder
subject: math
concept: Slice big multiplications into rectangles at place-value breaks (23 x 14 is four pieces), add the pieces back, and divide by building the missing side of a rectangle until the area is used up.

title: Road Trip Logbook
subject: math
concept: Log a family road trip's mileage in columns: add each day's miles and subtract to find what is left, regroup like an odometer rolling over, and check each answer with an estimate.

title: Fraction Wall Duel
subject: math
concept: Play fraction cards against a rival on a shared fraction wall: the bigger fraction wins, an equal one steals, and each win needs a reason the wall can show (common pieces, common count or the half line).

title: Recipe Scaler
subject: math
concept: Scale a family cornbread recipe for the class party using only one-size scoops: every amount becomes a count of unit fractions, like amounts add and subtract, and 6 batches is 6 times the scoops.

title: Money and Meters
subject: math
concept: One amount in four linked views (dimes and pennies, a meter stick, a 10 by 10 grid, a number line): change one and the rest follow, then compare decimals like 0.45 and 0.5 with proof.

title: Unit Ladder
subject: math
concept: Climb a conversion ladder where each rung adds a row to the table (1 ft = 12 in, 2 ft = 24 in) against your ghost, then use the table at a track meet to solve distance, time and liquid problems on a number line.

title: Community Plot Planner
subject: math
concept: Lay out a community garden where each family's plot has a set area or fence length, find the missing side (a 48 square foot plot that is 6 feet wide), and see why the formulas work.

title: Skate Park Angles
subject: math
concept: Build a skate park where every turn is a fraction of 360 degrees: add combo turns, find missing ones, measure ramps with a protractor, and log jump heights in eighths of a foot on a line plot.

title: Quilt Block Studio
subject: math
concept: Design quilt blocks with a drafting kit of points, segments, rays and lines; a mirror line finishes each half block, and a pattern label names its parallel and perpendicular lines, angle types and lines of symmetry.

title: Expression Escape
subject: math
concept: Escape a clockmaker's workshop: place parentheses and brackets to make each lock's code, build expressions from his spoken notes, and say which drawer holds more without computing.

title: Two Rule Race
subject: math
concept: Two snails follow different rules; plot their positions and see their relationship on the coordinate grid.

title: Zoom by Tens
subject: math
concept: Zoom into a meter stick through tenths, hundredths and thousandths to measure a ladybug, a rice grain and a feather; each zoom is a power of ten, and the decimal point slides as you go.

title: Grocery Run
subject: math
concept: Plan the food for a 28-student field day on a $120 budget: multiply packs and prices, divide bulk packs into servings, compare unit prices, and catch the error on the receipt.

title: Fraction Kitchen
subject: math
concept: Hit exact amounts by pouring from different-size cups into a bowl you mark in shared pieces, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes sixths; estimate every pour first and fix a helper's 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7.

title: Shrink Ray
subject: math
concept: Predict whether the ray's fraction dial will shrink or grow a picture before you fire, then tile the new rectangle to see why 2/3 x 3/4 is 6/12, and take scaling jobs from the neighborhood.

title: Camp Cook Share-Out
subject: math
concept: Share pans and scoops at camp: 3 pans for 4 tables gives each 3/4 of a pan, half a pan splits among 3 tables, and the cook counts quarter-cup scoops in 2 cups, so fractions are division and dividing by a unit fraction makes sense.

title: Seed Sprout Data
subject: math
concept: Run a windowsill bean experiment: measure seedlings to the nearest 1/8 inch, stack them on a line plot, share uneven water equally among pots, and convert cups to quarts and inches to feet to plan a month of care.

title: Box Packer
subject: math
concept: Pack unit cubes into food-bank crates one at a time, then a layer at a time, until length x width x height falls out; rotate boxes to see the order does not matter, and split L-shaped crates into two boxes.

title: Sea Search Grid
subject: math
concept: Join a harbor rescue crew: mark radio positions as (east, north) from the harbor, call search points to find a drifting kayak from "3 east, 2 south" replies, and read a drift log on the grid.

title: Shape Sieve
subject: math
concept: Quadrilaterals and triangles drop through sieves (four sides, parallel pairs, right angles, equal sides) and stop at the most specific name they earn; predict where a square lands, then build a hierarchy where every shape keeps its parents' properties.

title: Smoothie Lab
subject: math
concept: Mix fruit in ratios and taste-test (the tool reacts); find recipes that taste the same at bigger sizes.

title: How Many Fit?
subject: math
concept: Drag fraction bars into a container to see how many 3/4s fit in 2/3, read the part bar as 8/9 of a divisor, and solve sharing and missing-side stories until the flip-and-multiply shortcut explains itself.

title: Factor Forge
subject: math
concept: Smash numbers into prime factors; matching factors between two numbers forge their GCF and LCM.

title: Deep Sea Dive
subject: math
concept: Map a coast in cross-section with sea level at 0: place divers and gulls on a vertical number line, compare order and distance from the surface, then plot sea life in all four quadrants and reflect points across the water.

title: Expression Garden
subject: math
concept: Lay out a community garden with beds sized by expressions (x-rows, square beds, cube planters); regroup 3(x + 2) into 3x + 6, evaluate with a plant counter, and learn that one matching value does not make two gardens equivalent.

title: Balance Puzzle
subject: math
concept: Find what's in sealed sacks at a farmers market scale by removing equal weights or splitting into equal groups; when the scale tips instead of leveling, write the inequality and shade every weight that could be inside.

title: Summer Stand
subject: math
concept: Run a summer drink stand where cups sold and money earned move together in a table, graph and equation; name which quantity depends on which, find profit after supplies, and compare it with babysitting at $12 an hour.

title: Net Folder
subject: math
concept: Design a board game's box and pyramid pieces: draw nets from coordinates, find each face's area and the total cardboard, fold them, and fill the box with half-inch cubes to see why l x w x h still works with fractions.

title: Sign Shop
subject: math
concept: Price the paint for odd-shaped signs by cutting and sliding pieces: a parallelogram becomes a rectangle, a trapezoid becomes two triangles and a rectangle, and composite signs split into shapes you know.

title: Question Lab
subject: math
concept: Sort questions by asking "would the answers vary?", rewrite non-statistical ones, then send your own question to a simulated grade 6 class and describe the center, spread and shape of the answers.

title: Box Plot Builder
subject: math
concept: Switch real temperature and sports data between dot plot, histogram and box plot, report median, mean, IQR and MAD, and drag one point to watch the mean chase an outlier while the median holds still.

title: Tax and Tip
subject: math
concept: Run a diner register for a week: tax and tips line up through the origin while a flat fee does not; find the constant in every receipt, then work discounts, price rises, percent error and a simple-interest loan.

title: Hot Air and Sandbags
subject: math
concept: Fly a balloon where hot-air puffs are +1 and sandbags are -1: removing a sandbag lifts you, removing three groups of two sandbags shows -3 x -2 = +6, and missions mix fractions and decimals.

title: Remainder Loop
subject: math
concept: Divide 1 by 7 the long way and watch the remainders cycle, then try other fractions and find out why every fraction's decimal must end or repeat.

title: Expression Match
subject: math
concept: Win pairs against a rival by rewriting your expression into one on the table with move cards (distribute, factor, combine), then read what each form tells you, like a + 0.05a and 1.05a for a 5% raise.

title: Phone Plan Showdown
subject: math
concept: Play a skeptical customer at a phone store: turn each sales claim into an equation or inequality, solve it, graph the solutions, and say exactly when Plan B really is cheaper.

title: Blueprint Studio
subject: math
concept: Design a bedroom on a scale floor plan, check the fit in 3D, redraw it at a new scale (area grows by the square), and build corner-desk triangles from given sides and angles to see when they make one triangle, many or none.

title: Clay Cutting Bench
subject: math
concept: Slice clay prisms and pyramids with a wire at different angles and predict each cut face before it opens.

title: Big Wheel, Small Wheel
subject: math
concept: Settle round-object arguments (one 18-inch pizza or two 12-inch ones?) by rolling wheels to find pi and cutting circles into wedges to see why A = pi r squared grows faster than you expect.

title: Intersection Angles
subject: math
concept: Find missing angles at a busy intersection where crossing streets, rail crossings and scissor gates make vertical, adjacent, supplementary and complementary angles, writing and solving an equation for each.

title: Aquarium Builder
subject: math
concept: Plan composite prism tanks and planter boxes: buy the glass (surface area) and fill the water (volume) for shapes built from cubes and right prisms.

title: Jellybean Jar
subject: math
concept: Estimate a giant jar's color mix from scoops: an unstirred top scoop is biased, random scoops are fair, many scoops show how much estimates wobble, and two candy makers' jars are compared by bean weight.

title: Carnival Odds
subject: math
concept: Inspect a school carnival's games for fairness: place each chance from 0 to 1, run booths ten and ten thousand times, compare results to the model to catch a rigged wheel, and use trees and simulations for two-step games.

title: Square Root Hunt
subject: math
concept: Trap numbers on a zooming number line: catch repeating decimals as fractions, then squeeze the square root of 2 between ever-closer decimals that never repeat, and use the squeezes to compare and place irrational numbers.

title: Size of Everything
subject: math
concept: From a virus to the Milky Way: compare sizes in scientific notation on a slider through scales.

title: Ski Slope Designer
subject: math
concept: Lay out ski runs on a mountain profile graph: test steepness with a skier, draw slope triangles anywhere to see they are similar, compare runs given as graphs, equations and tables, and start one at a lodge to get y = mx + b.

title: Two Trains
subject: math
concept: Two trains, two equations, one graph; drag speeds and start times to see where (and if) they meet.

title: Function Machine Factory
subject: math
concept: Work quality control at a factory of input-output machines: reject any machine with two outputs for one input, compare machines given as tables, graphs, equations and words, and sort straight-line machines from curved ones.

title: Story Graphs
subject: math
concept: Match short life stories to the graphs that tell them, sketch graphs from new stories, and turn steady stories into linear models by finding where they start and how fast they change.

title: Transformation Dock
subject: math
concept: An L-shaped cargo tile must land on its outline; slide, flip, turn and resize it, replay the route as coordinate rules, decide which docks are congruent or only similar, then tile triangles to see why angles sum to 180.

title: Square Slicer
subject: math
concept: Cut the squares on a right triangle's short sides and slide the pieces to fill the big square, then use the theorem to square a deck corner, fit a pole in a box, and measure shortcuts on a park map grid.

title: Snow Globe Maker
subject: math
concept: Run a winter craft-fair booth making snow globes, cone candle molds and cylinder bases: pour tests reveal the volume formulas, then volume sets the water, wax and glitter each piece needs and what it costs.

title: Data Detective
subject: math
concept: Solve cases with real paired data (foot length vs height, geyser wait vs eruption): read the scatter's pattern, fit a line by eye, use its slope and intercept to predict, and crack a two-way table.

title: Exponent Rule Builder
subject: math
concept: Unlock exponent rules by experimenting with patterns, then prove why a 1/2 power is a square root.

title: Unit Sense
subject: math
concept: Real headlines with impossible numbers; use dimensional analysis to find which claims fall apart.

title: Algebra Tile Studio
subject: math
concept: Factor and complete the square with algebra tiles; watch the rectangle and the expression change together.

title: Polynomials as Numbers
subject: math
concept: Set x = 10 and watch every polynomial become an ordinary number; multiplying polynomials turns into long multiplication without carrying, and like terms line up like place-value columns.

title: Model My World
subject: math
concept: Pick a real situation (phone data, gym fees, savings) and write the equation that predicts it; the tool checks it against data.

title: Equation Golf
subject: math
concept: Solve equations in as few legal moves as possible; par scores reward elegant solutions.

title: Intersection Quest
subject: math
concept: Find where two lines cross three ways (graph, substitution, elimination) and race your own best time.

title: Graph Story Lab
subject: math
concept: Explore real graphs (a day of temperatures, a roller coaster) and label domain, range, max and intervals.

title: Which Model Wins?
subject: math
concept: Real data sets (viral videos, braking distance, savings): fit linear, quadratic and exponential models and pick the best.

title: Launch Pad
subject: math
concept: Launch a projectile and see its quadratic; the roots are where it lands. Solve to aim for targets.

title: Correlation Guessing Game
subject: math
concept: Guess the correlation of a scatter plot; residual plots expose the trick ones.

title: Rigid Motion Twins
subject: math
concept: Each level shows a shape and its twin; map one onto the other with the fewest rigid motions, then write the sequence as the proof that they are congruent.

title: Proof Tower
subject: math
concept: Drag statements and reasons into a proof that holds up; a compass-and-straightedge sandbox handles constructions.

title: Shadow Measure
subject: math
concept: Measure a flagpole with its shadow and a meter stick using similar triangles, then check with the real height.

title: Ramp and Roof
subject: math
concept: Design accessible ramps and roof pitches that meet code using sine, cosine and tangent.

title: Circle Theorem Explorer
subject: math
concept: Drag points around circles and watch inscribed angles, chords and tangents keep their relationships.

title: Coordinate Proof Lab
subject: math
concept: Place shapes on the grid and prove they're parallelograms or rectangles with slopes and distances.

title: Slice and Stack
subject: math
concept: Slice 3D solids with a moving plane and see the cross sections; spin shapes to make solids of rotation.

title: Packaging Challenge
subject: math
concept: Design a can or box that holds a given volume with the least material; compare against real products.

title: Medical Test Paradox
subject: math
concept: Run a population through a disease test; conditional probability shows why a positive result isn't the whole story.

title: Imaginary Island
subject: math
concept: Explore the complex plane as an island map; multiplication by i rotates you a quarter turn.

title: Rollercoaster Polynomials
subject: math
concept: Design a coaster track by choosing zeros and degree; the ride has to start and end at ground level.

title: Work Rate Crew
subject: math
concept: Schedule painting crews working at different rates; rational equations decide how long jobs take together.

title: Outbreak Model
subject: math
concept: Model a spreading rumor or virus; logarithms answer "when will it reach 1 million?"

title: Ferris Wheel
subject: math
concept: Ride a Ferris wheel and watch height trace a sine wave; change radius and speed to change the graph.

title: Undo Machine
subject: math
concept: Chain function machines, then build the machine that undoes them. Some machines can't be undone.

title: Savings Plan
subject: math
concept: Compare saving plans (add $10 a week vs double a penny a day); sequences and series show who wins and when.

title: Poll Workshop
subject: math
concept: Design a poll, pick a sample method, and see how bias and margin of error change the headline.

title: Function Family Reunion
subject: math
concept: Meet the parent functions and their transformed relatives; sliders show what each parameter does.

title: Identity Proof Race
subject: math
concept: Race to prove identities with drag-and-drop algebra steps; multiple routes to the same proof are celebrated.

title: Flight Planner
subject: math
concept: Fly a plane through crosswinds; add velocity vectors to land on the runway.

title: Image Transformer
subject: math
concept: Apply matrices to a photo to rotate, shear and stretch it; see why the order of multiplication matters.

title: Polar Rose Studio
subject: math
concept: Draw roses, spirals and cardioids with polar equations; export your art.

title: Conic Focus Finder
subject: math
concept: Slice a double cone at different angles to get circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas; see real-world uses.

title: Zoom to the Limit
subject: math
concept: Zoom into a curve until it looks straight; secant lines slide into a tangent.

title: Data Desk: Distributions
subject: math
concept: Real public data sets; describe shape, center, spread and unusual features with guided prompts.

title: Design the Study
subject: math
concept: Test whether energy drinks really speed up reaction times: choose random assignment, a control group, blinding and a placebo, and a skeptical journal editor shows how each missing piece lets a hidden variable fake the result. Surveys and sampling stay with poll-workshop.

title: Game Show Strategist
subject: math
concept: Simulate game show choices (Monty Hall and friends); expected value says when to switch.

title: Sample Machine
subject: math
concept: Draw thousands of samples and watch a sampling distribution form; the Central Limit Theorem appears on its own.

title: Courtroom Statistics
subject: math
concept: Put a claim on trial: the null is innocent until data proves otherwise. P-values become evidence.

title: Fair Dice Investigation
subject: math
concept: Is the casino's die loaded? Collect counts and run chi-square to decide; then test whether a slope is real.

title: Hole Hunter
subject: math
concept: Find the holes, jumps and asymptotes hidden in graphs; repair them to make the function continuous.

title: Speedometer
subject: math
concept: Drive a car along a position graph; the speedometer is the derivative, drawn live.

title: Optimization Workshop
subject: math
concept: Fence the biggest field, design the cheapest can; derivatives find the best design, and a slider proves it.

title: Rain Gauge
subject: math
concept: Rainfall rate over a day fills a tank; Riemann rectangles approximate the total as they get thinner.

title: Solid Spinner
subject: math
concept: Spin regions around an axis to make solids; stack disks and washers to find volume.

title: Slope Field Garden
subject: math
concept: Plant seeds in a slope field and watch solution curves grow; model population and cooling.

title: Fire Lookout Triangles
subject: math
concept: Two fire lookouts spot the same smoke; use their bearings and the distance between towers to find the fire with the law of sines, then a third tower checks the answer with the law of cosines.

title: Push the Pumpkin
subject: science
concept: Push or pull a pumpkin, a ball and a wagon with small and big pushes from either side, compare how far and which way each rolls, then place ramps and bales to steer a ball into the barn.

title: Shade Builder
subject: science
concept: Feel which backyard spots the sun warmed, then shade the sandbox with umbrellas, a tree, a tent or a sail; a heat camera shows which spots stay cool, and two designs are compared to pick the better one.

title: Terrarium Pal
subject: science
concept: Care for a terrarium with a plant, a snail and a pill bug over a sped-up week, giving or holding back water, light, food and air, and find what every living thing needs and what only plants or animals need.

title: Weather Wardrobe
subject: science
concept: Look outside and stamp today's weather, dress a character to match, and watch a picture calendar show patterns over the months; a storm forecast shows how people use forecasts to get ready.

title: Beaver Builders
subject: science
concept: Help a beaver family dam a stream and watch it become a pond that new animals move into, then help a family nearby choose ways to share the valley and take less from it.

title: Vibration Station
subject: science
concept: Pluck rubber bands, tap a drum with rice on it and hum into a tube to see that shaking makes sound and sound makes things shake, then build a cup phone or drum signal to reach a friend far away.

title: Shadow Puppet Studio
subject: science
concept: Find out you can see in a dark room only when light shines, test cardboard, wax paper, clear plastic and foil in a flashlight beam, then use what each does to light up your own shadow puppet show.

title: Nature Inventor
subject: science
concept: Solve a person's problem by copying a plant or animal part (burr hooks, thick fur, a strong beak); study how the part helps it survive, build a gadget from the idea and test it.

title: Who's My Baby?
subject: science
concept: Match each baby plant or animal to its parent by spotting what is alike and what is not exactly alike; care cards show how parents feed, warm, protect and teach their young.

title: Sky Diary
subject: science
concept: Speed up the sky over a backyard for a day, a month and a year, predict where the sun and moon will be next, and compare daylight hours on a winter day and a summer day.

title: Three Pigs Lab
subject: science
concept: Test straw, sticks and bricks (and more) for strength, flexibility and waterproofing to build the best house.

title: Melt or Not?
subject: science
concept: Sort changes into "can go back" (melting ice, freezing juice) and "can't go back" (baking a cake, burning paper).

title: Plant Experiment Shelf
subject: science
concept: Run a fair test on four bean plants with and without light and water and measure two weeks of growth, then build a fuzzy model animal and test how well it carries pollen and seeds.

title: Habitat Hunt
subject: science
concept: Explore a rainforest, desert, pond and backyard; count species and compare biodiversity.

title: Fast or Slow?
subject: science
concept: Place real Earth changes (a landslide, an eruption, a canyon, a shrinking beach) on a timeline from seconds to millions of years using clues from clips and photos, then compare ways to protect land from wind and water.

title: Island Maker
subject: science
concept: Sculpt an island with mountains, rivers, lakes, bays and a glacier, then turn it into a map with a key and find where its water is and whether it is liquid or frozen.

title: Tug of War Arena
subject: science
concept: Add pullers to a tug of war and read the force arrows to see balanced pulls hold still and unbalanced ones move, then time a swing and a rolling marble and use the pattern to predict their next position.

title: Magnet Maze
subject: science
concept: Steer a steel ball through mazes with magnets you never touch to it, test how distance, poles and materials change the pull, try static levels with a balloon, then define and solve your own magnet design problem.

title: Life Cycle Wheel
subject: science
concept: Sort stage cards into life cycle wheels for a frog, a butterfly, a bean, a chicken and a human, then line them up to see every cycle differs but all share birth, growth, reproduction and death.

title: Wolf Pack Survival
subject: science
concept: Run seasons for wolves, sardines and honeybees living alone or in groups, read the survival tallies, and build an argument with evidence about how groups help members survive and what a group costs.

title: Puppy Traits
subject: science
concept: Meet a puppy litter and sort its traits into those from parents and those shaped by food and training, then watch pale and dark mice on sand and soil to see how small differences help some survive.

title: Fossil Clues
subject: science
concept: Split rock slabs in a dry Wyoming basin to find fossil fish and palm leaves, work out that a warm lake was there long ago, sort which animals survive there today, and judge solutions for pronghorn crossing a highway.

title: Climate Postcards
subject: science
concept: Graph real monthly temperature and rain for cities around the world, describe each climate on a postcard and why it differs, then judge which designs best protect each city from its weather hazard.

title: Bowling Lab
subject: science
concept: Roll a ball from different ramp heights into bowling pins, measure its speed and how far the pins fly, and predict where the energy goes when ball meets pins.

title: Contraption Workshop
subject: science
concept: Build a chain machine that rings a bell by linking parts that change energy from one form to another; an energy view shows energy traveling by current, light and sound, and fair tests find the weak link.

title: Secret Code Signals
subject: science
concept: Make waves in a lake to see amplitude, wavelength and a buoy bobbing in place, then send messages across the water with flashes, beeps and wave patterns, invent your own code and compare which works best.

title: How Animals See
subject: science
concept: See the world through the eyes of a bee, an owl and a snake; explore the structures that make it possible.

title: Canyon Reader
subject: science
concept: Hike down the Grand Canyon layer by layer, read each rock's fossils and patterns as clues, and solve how the place changed from sea to desert to sea before the river cut through it.

title: Erosion Table
subject: science
concept: Run a sand table with water, wind, ice and plant controls, change one thing at a time over fast-forwarded seasons, and measure how fast each one weathers rock and carves land.

title: World Layers Map
subject: science
concept: Turn on world map layers (mountains, ocean trenches, volcanoes, earthquakes, ocean depth) and find that they line up in patterns, like the ring around the Pacific; the plate explanation waits for grade 6.

title: Town Planner: Disaster Ready
subject: science
concept: Run a coastal river town for twenty years, choose its energy sources and see what each takes from the land and air, and compare ways to protect people from floods, earthquakes, a tsunami and volcanic ash.

title: Particle Zoom
subject: science
concept: Zoom from a kitchen counter into dissolving sugar, an inflating balloon and melting ice to see particles too small to see, and weigh each change before and after to find the total weight stays the same.

title: Mystery Powders
subject: science
concept: Identify five unlabeled white powders and a mystery mix by testing them with water, vinegar, iodine, a magnet and a conductivity tester, and decide which mixes make a new substance.

title: Which Way Is Down?
subject: science
concept: Drop an apple at schools in Alaska, Ecuador, Australia and Antarctica, record which way it falls, then zoom out to see every down points to Earth's center and argue that gravity pulls toward it.

title: Living Pond
subject: science
concept: Stock a pond with algae, snails, minnows, dragonflies, a turtle and a heron, then let the seasons run: populations boom and crash on real predator-prey math, matter loops through decomposers while sunlight energy flows one way, and pulling out one species makes the pond wobble two seasons later.

title: Shadow Clock
subject: science
concept: Chalk a stick's shadow every hour on four days of the year, graph its length and direction, log which star groups are up at night, then explain each pattern with Earth's spin and orbit.

title: Star Lanterns
subject: science
concept: Carry identical lanterns farther and farther across a dark field and measure how dim they look, then find that the sun looks brightest only because it is the closest star.

title: Sphere Connections
subject: science
concept: Card game where each event sets off the next across rock, water, air and life (volcano to ash to rain to forest); fresh water is the scarce currency, held in a bank with Earth's real proportions.

title: Community Solutions
subject: science
concept: Read real case files on how communities used science to protect water, soil and wildlife, combine two ideas into a plan for a river town, then answer residents' questions at the town meeting.

title: Moon Phase Model
subject: science
concept: Orbit the Moon around Earth and watch phases and eclipses from both a space and a backyard view.

title: Pocket Universe
subject: science
concept: Fling stars, planets, moons and comets into empty space and let real gravity take over: build a two-sun system, slingshot a probe past three planets, rescue a moon that keeps crashing; glowing trails and a time scrubber show why orbits are ellipses, then load our real solar system to scale.

title: Earth's Calendar
subject: science
concept: Match fossils to stack rock layers from three places, mark where life changes most, and watch the marks become the eras of the time scale; then squeeze 4.6 billion years into one calendar year.

title: Plate Puzzle
subject: science
concept: Fit continents back together using fossils, rocks and coastlines; then run the plates forward and backward in time.

title: Rock Recycler
subject: science
concept: Follow one mineral grain through melting, cooling, weathering, burial and uplift, powered by the sun and Earth's inner heat, with each step on its real clock, from a landslide in seconds to uplift over millions of years.

title: Raindrop's Journey
subject: science
concept: Follow a water molecule through evaporation, clouds, rivers and glaciers; its choices are physics.

title: Front Line
subject: science
concept: Collect readings from a row of weather stations as a cold air mass meets a warm one, then use the data to forecast tomorrow's weather.

title: Ocean Conveyor
subject: science
concept: Heat the equator, set Earth spinning and watch winds, ocean gyres and the deep salty conveyor form; then compare two coasts at the same latitude whose currents give them very different climates.

title: Cooler Challenge
subject: science
concept: Build a lunchbox cooler from insulation and pick the cold packs inside, then run a hot-car test; the graph shows how layers slow heat and how mass and material change how fast lunch warms.

title: Cell City
subject: science
concept: Check real micrographs to find which samples are made of cells, then zoom from the body through organs and tissues into one cell, where each organelle's job is shown, with a city overlay you can switch on.

title: Molecule Forge
subject: science
concept: Snap atoms together by real bonding rules (fill every bonding spot) and grow a collection from water, methane and ammonia up to caffeine, then repeat a pattern to grow salt, diamond and copper and see why each behaves as it does.

title: Made From
subject: science
concept: Trace an everyday synthetic material (a nylon jacket, a plastic bottle, a medicine) back to the natural resource it came from and forward to its effects on society.

title: Particle Party
subject: science
concept: Heat and cool particles and watch them shift between solid, liquid and gas; the temperature graph explains the plateaus.

title: Reaction Kitchen
subject: science
concept: Three kitchen benches: test whether baking soda and vinegar made something new, weigh a sealed bag to find mass conserved as atoms rearrange, then design a hand warmer that runs on rusting iron.

title: Leaf Factory
subject: science
concept: Run a leaf as a factory: take in light, water and carbon dioxide, make sugar, then spend it to grow, store or burn at night; follow one carbon atom into a caterpillar that eats the leaf.

title: Predator-Prey Island
subject: science
concept: Run Isle Royale's real wolves and moose, test what explains each rise and crash in decades of winter counts, then predict competition, predation and partnership patterns in other ecosystems.

title: Energy Pyramid
subject: science
concept: Build a grassland energy pyramid: about a tenth of each level's energy feeds the next and the rest leaves as heat, while an atom view shows matter looping back through decomposers.

title: Invasive Species Alert
subject: science
concept: Zebra mussels turn up in a small lake; over ten years pick responses scored on cost, biodiversity and clean water, and watch native species, fishing and the town's water intake respond.

title: Resource Map
subject: science
concept: Map where minerals, fossil fuels and groundwater are found and why; see how geology decides where resources are.

title: Crash Test Lab
subject: science
concept: Collide carts of different masses with force meters on both bumpers, plan push tests that change force or mass, then design a bumper that keeps an egg passenger safe.

title: Electromagnet Lab
subject: science
concept: Build an electromagnet, ask which changes make it pull harder (turns, batteries, core, distance), test each one, then map its invisible field with a compass and compare a charged balloon's pull.

title: Half-Pipe Energy
subject: science
concept: Draw a ramp and drop a skater: kinetic and potential energy trade places in a live bar chart, friction turns some into heat, and your runs graph how mass and speed set kinetic energy.

title: Wave Tank
subject: science
concept: Make waves in a tank, on a rope and with a light beam; change amplitude and frequency and measure what they do, then set mirrors, glass, foam and tile in the way to see waves reflect, pass or fade.

title: Copy of a Copy
subject: science
concept: Send the same message as a smooth analog wave and as digital pulses through a chain of noisy relays, and see which arrives intact.

title: Gene Pool
subject: science
concept: Grow strawberries by runners and by seeds: clones match while seedlings vary, sun and water change growth, a mutation changes a protein and a trait, then cross plants like a breeder to bring out bigger, sweeter fruit.

title: Flower Lure
subject: science
concept: Design a flower's color, scent, shape and nectar to win visits from a chosen pollinator, then compare animal behaviors (songs, nest building, guarding young) that raise the odds of reproducing.

title: Bug Hunt
subject: science
concept: Be a bird hunting moths on tree bark; the moths you miss breed, the bark turns sooty or clean, and a graph of moth colors across generations shows natural selection as it happened to England's peppered moths.

title: Fossil and Bone Bench
subject: science
concept: Order fossils through rock layers to find patterns of change, compare limb bones (a whale flipper, a bat wing, a human arm), and compare early embryos across species.

title: Hazard Forecaster
subject: science
concept: Filter real earthquake, hurricane and wildfire records by place, season and size, place a few warning sensors where the patterns point, then test them against years the data held back.

title: Town Footprint
subject: science
concept: Watch a town's water, land and energy use grow with its population and spending, then design a way to monitor and shrink one impact.

title: Warming Evidence Desk
subject: science
concept: Ask questions of real records (temperature, carbon dioxide, the sun's output, volcanoes) to sort out which factors explain the rise in global temperature over the past century.

title: Span and Spire
subject: science
concept: Design truss bridges for a farm-road creek crossing on a budget, from criteria the people who use it set; trucks roll across while every member glows from blue to red with stress and the weakest buckles in slow motion, then build towers against wind and a shake table, compare designs and combine the best parts.

title: Membrane Gatekeeper
subject: science
concept: Be the cell membrane: let in what the cell needs and block what it doesn't, as traffic speeds up.

title: Body Thermostat
subject: science
concept: Keep a body at 37 C through exercise, cold and fever; feedback loops kick in automatically.

title: Mitosis Mixer
subject: science
concept: Sort scrambled microscope images into the stages of mitosis; then see stem cells specialize.

title: Energy Accountant
subject: science
concept: Track carbon and energy through photosynthesis and respiration with a ledger; the books have to balance, and switching the oxygen off shows how little energy fermentation pays.

title: Protein Factory
subject: science
concept: Transcribe DNA to mRNA and translate codons into amino acids; a single mutation can break the protein.

title: Punnett Predictor
subject: science
concept: Cross parents and compare Punnett predictions to 1,000 simulated offspring; probability made visible.

title: Tree of Life
subject: science
concept: Explore an interactive tree of life; compare anatomy, DNA and fossils to see shared ancestry.

title: Carrying Capacity
subject: science
concept: Grow a deer population with limited food and predators; see logistic growth level off.

title: Reserve Designer
subject: science
concept: Design a nature reserve with a limited budget; balance habitat corridors, farms and towns.

title: Star Life Story
subject: science
concept: Follow stars of different masses from birth to death; see where elements are forged.

title: Orbit Lab
subject: science
concept: Change mass and speed to explore Kepler's laws with real planet data.

title: Feedback Loop Builder
subject: science
concept: Connect ice, albedo, temperature and carbon in a causal loop; see which loops amplify and which stabilize, then add life: plankton and forests change the air, and the air changes what can live.

title: Water Shapes Earth
subject: science
concept: Freeze-thaw rocks, dissolve limestone and carve with rivers; water's properties explain the changes.

title: Climate Dashboard
subject: science
concept: Real temperature, CO2 and ice data with filters; separate long-term trends from weather noise.

title: Lake Commons
subject: science
concept: Run a lake town for 100 years in five-year turns: set the fishing boats, forest cuts, new homes and energy, then live through floods and droughts; take about what grows back or watch the lake empty.

title: Elements Inspector
subject: science
concept: EXISTING TOOL (Beta). Explore every element: 3D atom model, family, properties and emission spectra.

title: Bond Battle
subject: science
concept: Card game where atoms bond ionically or covalently; intermolecular forces decide which substances boil first.

title: Equation Balancer
subject: science
concept: Balance equations by adding molecules on both sides; atoms on the scale must match.

title: Mole Bakery
subject: science
concept: Bake by the mole: scale recipes (reactions), find the limiting ingredient and maximize yield.

title: Hand Warmer Lab
subject: science
concept: Design a hand warmer or cold pack by choosing reactions; measure temperature change and bond energies.

title: Equilibrium Seesaw
subject: science
concept: Stress a reaction with heat, pressure and concentration; watch it shift back (Le Chatelier).

title: Gas Law Lab
subject: science
concept: A piston, a balloon and a thermometer; change pressure, volume and temperature and discover the gas laws.

title: pH Mystery Liquids
subject: science
concept: Identify household mystery liquids with indicators and pH probes; neutralize a spill safely.

title: Half-Life Dice
subject: science
concept: Roll thousands of atom dice to see half-life; date ancient artifacts with carbon-14.

title: Motion Graph Match
subject: science
concept: Move a character to match a target position or velocity graph; beat your best time.

title: Curling Stones
subject: science
concept: Slide stones of different masses with different pushes along the ice; F = ma predicts where each one stops, and sweeping changes the friction.

title: Collision Lab
subject: science
concept: Elastic and inelastic collisions on an air track; conserve momentum and design a crumple zone.

title: Field Lines
subject: science
concept: Place masses and charges and see gravitational and electric fields; compare the inverse square laws.

title: Zipline Energy
subject: science
concept: Design a zipline from a cliff platform to a far tree; with friction on, energy conservation decides whether the rider reaches the far platform and how hard the brake has to work.

title: Circuit Builder
subject: science
concept: Build circuits with batteries, resistors and bulbs; measure current and voltage and make a generator spin.

title: Sound Studio
subject: science
concept: Synthesize sounds by mixing waves; see frequency, wavelength and harmonics on a scope.

title: Spectrum Explorer
subject: science
concept: Slide across the EM spectrum from radio to gamma; see what each wavelength does in tech and the body.

title: Biome Atlas
subject: science
concept: Explore world biomes with climate charts; predict which biome forms from temperature and rainfall.

title: Population Dashboard
subject: science
concept: Real population and resource-use data by country; compare footprints and project the future.

title: Grid Operator
subject: science
concept: Keep a city's lights on from the grid control room, mixing coal, gas, solar, wind and nuclear; balance cost, reliability and emissions through a heat wave and a still, cloudy week.

title: Up the Watershed
subject: science
concept: Trace a river's pollution back to its sources with water tests; propose and test solutions.

title: Design Challenge Studio
subject: science
concept: Tackle a global challenge (clean water, cooling) by breaking it down, prototyping and weighing tradeoffs.

title: Nerve Signal Relay
subject: science
concept: Race your own reaction time: tap when a light flashes or a tone sounds, watch the signal travel from eye or ear to brain to finger, and see practice make a sequence faster while a new choice stays slow.

title: Hot Meets Cold
subject: science
concept: Drop a hot metal block into cold water and predict the final temperature; jiggling particles trade energy until both sides match, and no setting ever makes the heat flow back.

title: Playground Rules
subject: social-studies
concept: Hang rule signs on a busy playground with no rules and watch the scene replay calmer; give each rule its reason, then decide a new swing rule with illustrated classmates by listening and voting.

title: Me on the Map
subject: social-studies
concept: Zoom out from a bedroom to a house, street, town, state, country and planet; kids point out each level.

title: Then and Now Flip
subject: social-studies
concept: Flip picture pairs (phones, classrooms, toys) to sort then from now, then line up three versions of one thing from Grandma's time to today and compare a long-ago kid's day with yours.

title: Backpack Pack
subject: social-studies
concept: Pack a camping backpack with only six pockets; each item you add means leaving another behind, and the trip shows which were needs and which were wants.

title: Symbol Spotter
subject: social-studies
concept: Find national symbols on everyday things (a coin, a stamp, a flag, a postcard), hear the idea each stands for (freedom, fairness, welcome), then open holidays that honor people who changed the country and ask your own questions.

title: Community Helpers Village
subject: social-studies
concept: Place helpers around a village (baker, mail carrier, firefighter, librarian, a snow-shoveling neighbor) and remove one to see what breaks; learn which the town pays for, how each earns a living, and how everyone shares a snow day.

title: Compass Rose Quest
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow compass directions and a map key across a park to find treasure, telling natural features from built ones, then make your own room map with a key and clues and watch a parrot try to follow it.

title: My Life Timeline
subject: social-studies
concept: Help Juno put her life in order from a shoebox of keepsakes (a baby photo, a tiny shoe, a birthday card, Grandpa's story), naming each kind of source, then build your own life timeline from stickers and drawings.

title: Market Day
subject: social-studies
concept: With five tokens, the class shops a weekend market as consumers; each stall sells a good or offers a service, every choice means giving something else up, and the stall owners explain what they made or did.

title: Festival Parade
subject: social-studies
concept: Floats from real festivals roll past; guess each celebration from its food, music, clothes and season, hear a kid who celebrates it, and follow the map to see how it traveled with the people who carried it.

title: Town Council
subject: social-studies
concept: Sit on the town council as the empty lot becomes a park or a parking lot; hear neighbors who disagree, speak in turn, learn what the mayor and council each decide, and vote on a compromise.

title: Three Towns
subject: social-studies
concept: Sort homes, jobs and transport into a city, a suburb and a farm town, then trace one breakfast in each to see what comes from nearby and what from far away, and how each town's land shapes its work.

title: Changemaker Cards
subject: social-studies
concept: Collect cards of real people who improved their communities; each starts face down with a "before" picture, and asking who, what, why and how flips it, then the album lines up from long ago to today.

title: Piggy Bank Planner
subject: social-studies
concept: Save for a kite in the shop window: each week choose to spend, fill the piggy bank or visit the bank that keeps money safe and lends it out, and see why saving gets you more.

title: Resource Detective
subject: social-studies
concept: Trace everyday objects (pencil, T-shirt, juice) back to the natural resources they came from.

title: Map Maker
subject: social-studies
concept: Map a new town on an island seen only from a satellite photo, placing the port, farms and homes where the land suits them, with key, scale and grid; then a traveler follows your map and shows where it gets her lost.

title: Then-and-Now Overlay
subject: social-studies
concept: Slide back through one real Main Street in the 1890s, 1940s and today using public-domain insurance maps, photos and a directory; compare what each source tells you, and add your own town as an extra.

title: Promise Check
subject: social-studies
concept: A class president race and a town mayor race run side by side; check each promise against what that office can really do, help write an honest speech, vote by secret ballot, and compare how each place decides.

title: Paper Plane Assembly Line
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a paper plane shop for a school flying contest: split one worker's job into stations, buy a tool or train the crew, and watch output and profit grow until a sick day shows how much everyone depends on each other.

title: Day in the Life
subject: social-studies
concept: Spend a school day with kids in Kenya, Peru, Japan and Norway, seeing how homes, food and travel fit the land and weather, then find on a population map where most people live in each country and why.

title: State Story Timeline
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick your state and walk its story from the Native nations who lived there first to statehood and today; ask questions about who drove each change, link causes to effects, and compare a kid's life then and now.

title: State Quest
subject: social-studies
concept: EXISTING TOOL (Beta). Find all 50 states on a map in Practice or Challenge mode. Capitals and regions modes planned.

title: Bill to Law Board Game
subject: social-studies
concept: Carry a kid-proposed bill around a state capitol board through committees, both chambers, a veto and an override; learn what each office can do and where the rules come from, then see what the law changes.

title: State Economy Map
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick your state and stack layers of land, resources, farms and industries to find where jobs cluster and why, then follow your state's top products to the places that buy them and see what comes back.

title: Settle the Valley
subject: social-studies
concept: Over fifty years, place farms, homes, a mill and roads in a river valley where people already live, and watch land and people change each other, from cleared forests and worn soil to a flood that forces families to move.

title: Nations of North America
subject: social-studies
concept: A map of Native nations organized by region, with homes, foods and ways of life tied to the environment. Content reviewed with tribal education resources.

title: Ship's Log
subject: social-studies
concept: Plan a 1600s voyage: supplies, route and crew choices; meet the consequences for sailors and Indigenous people.

title: Revolution Road
subject: social-studies
concept: Walk from 1763 to the Treaty of Paris on four parallel lanes (Patriot, Loyalist, Native nations, enslaved and free Black Americans), link causes to effects, and explain why people living at the same time chose different sides.

title: Rights Match
subject: social-studies
concept: Hear why people refused to ratify the Constitution without a list of rights, then sort real-life scenarios into the amendment that protects them and name the principle each right stands on.

title: Colonial Trade Routes
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow real cargoes across the 1700s Atlantic from New England, the Middle Colonies, the South, the Caribbean and Britain; see who made each, including enslaved Africans, and how the trade changed the colonies over time.

title: Five Themes Field Trip
subject: social-studies
concept: Take a field trip through one river city: pin photos from five stops onto a base map you build layer by layer with the five themes, compare satellite images decades apart, and chart one pattern to explain where people built.

title: Hunter to Farmer
subject: social-studies
concept: Lead a band in the Fertile Crescent through twenty years of seasons: forage, tend wild wheat or plant fields, and watch food, people, work, health and homes change, then see farming begin separately around the world.

title: River Kingdom
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a farming kingdom on the steady Nile, then on the flood-prone Tigris and Euphrates: dig canals, store grain and carve laws in stone, and see how each river shaped its land, its work and its government.

title: Silk Road Traders
subject: social-studies
concept: Trade cards along the routes linking Han China, Central Asia and India: goods change hands, and ideas like Buddhism ride along faster where travel is easier; then sort what the trade changed and what stayed the same.

title: Agora Assembly
subject: social-studies
concept: As an Athenian citizen in 483 BCE, debate and vote on spending new silver, then take the same question to Sparta's council and assembly; compare who decided and how, and ask the people left out why Athens is remembered.

title: Rome: Republic to Empire
subject: social-studies
concept: Play a senator's family from 133 to 27 BCE through real turning points as power slides from Senate to generals to Augustus; sort what changed and what lasted, and map the causes of the Republic's fall.

title: Region Compare
subject: social-studies
concept: Ask why two world regions differ, then lay real population, rainfall, income and language data on maps and charts you choose; find what makes the regions alike and different, and how rivers and rain pull people in.

title: Constantinople Defense
subject: social-studies
concept: Guard Constantinople through real sieges from 626 to 1453, spending on walls, fleet, diplomacy and trade; sort what changed and what lasted over eight centuries, then weigh the many causes of the city's fall.

title: House of Wisdom
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow one book from Greek scrolls to Arabic translation in Abbasid Baghdad, onto paper from China and into Latin in Toledo; collect the ideas carried at each stop and map how knowledge survived by moving.

title: Salt and Gold Caravan
subject: social-studies
concept: Run caravans from the Saharan salt mines to Timbuktu and Mali's gold fields; learn why salt and gold were worth crossing a desert for, what every barrier cost, and how Mali's gold reached Cairo and beyond.

title: Mongol Messenger
subject: social-studies
concept: Race an urgent message across the Mongol Empire by the yam relay, swapping horses and showing your paiza; beat the slower old way, then see what the same roads carried and sort what the empire changed and what stayed local.

title: Manor Life
subject: social-studies
concept: Look after one household on a 1190s English manor (a peasant family, the lord's or a monk's); seasons, labor days, tithes and a crusade tax shape each life, and the same events look different from each place.

title: Tenochtitlan Builder
subject: social-studies
concept: Build Tenochtitlan on Lake Texcoco with chinampas, causeways, an aqueduct and a flood dike, test it against floods, hunger and thirst, then see how the Inca and Maya solved the same problems elsewhere.

title: Printing Press
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a 1500s print shop against a scribe copying by hand: set type, print pamphlets and ship them across Europe, then ask who made the change matter and sort what printing changed and what stayed the same.

title: Columbian Exchange
subject: social-studies
concept: Sort crops, animals and diseases by where they began, then send them across the Atlantic and watch diets, populations and plantations change on both sides, from potatoes in Europe to smallpox in the Americas and sugar's forced labor.

title: Colonial Newsroom
subject: social-studies
concept: Edit a Patriot paper and a Loyalist paper in 1765 and 1770: headline the Stamp Act and the King Street shooting from the same evidence, then compare real pages and find what each side, and the record, leaves out.

title: Constitutional Convention
subject: social-studies
concept: Play a delegate from a small or large state at the 1787 Convention: bargain over representation, the three branches and slavery's compromises, weigh your state's interests against shared principles, and see how the plan still shapes government today.

title: Two Parties
subject: social-studies
concept: A card game of the 1790s: lead Hamilton's Federalists or Jefferson's Republicans through fights over the bank, a whiskey tax and the Sedition Act, using newspapers and voters, and judge each law as a fix for a real problem.

title: Expansion Map
subject: social-studies
concept: Slide from 1803 to 1853 as US territory, trails, railroads and telegraph lines spread and Native nations' lands shrink; read dated voices at each event, name what shaped each view, and chain causes to effects.

title: Mill Town
subject: social-studies
concept: Leave the farm for an 1830s Lowell mill: choose how to work, save, strike and petition while machines make each worker far more productive, then weigh who gained and how workers pushed for reform.

title: Voices of Freedom
subject: social-studies
concept: Read real first-person sources from people who were enslaved, people who escaped and those who fought slavery; note what shaped each voice, trace causes toward the Civil War, and compare their ways of seeking change with today's. No game mechanics.

title: Civil War Map Room
subject: social-studies
concept: Step through an animated map of the Civil War's turning points, reading real letters from both sides at each stop, then rank the causes of Union victory and defend your top pick with evidence.

title: Reconstruction Amendments
subject: social-studies
concept: Open the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments: see what each promised, how it was carried out and how Jim Crow undermined it, who acted at each step, and how the same amendments were used again a century later.

title: Ideas That Spread
subject: social-studies
concept: Carry Enlightenment ideas across an Atlantic map to the American, French, Haitian and Spanish American revolutions; see how each place read them differently, weigh the other causes, then score the governments each revolution built.

title: Factory Floor
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a Lancashire cotton mill from 1760 to 1900; invest in machines and skills, watch output per worker climb, and see the town fill with migrants and the costs paid by workers and enslaved cotton growers.

title: Scramble for Africa
subject: social-studies
concept: Slide Africa's map from 1870 to 1914 and open each region's layers: African states, European motives, voices from all sides, resistance from Adwa to Maji Maji, and the borders and economies that last today.

title: Alliance Web
subject: social-studies
concept: Pull one thread in Europe's alliance system and watch the whole web pull nations into war.

title: Inflation Wallet
subject: social-studies
concept: Live as a Berlin family from 1919 to 1933: buy bread through hyperinflation and the Depression, vote in each election, then weigh which causes really ended Weimar democracy.

title: Remembrance Archive
subject: social-studies
