concept: Follow real people and places through the Holocaust and the war in documents, photographs and testimony; judge each source's maker, date and purpose to learn what happened and how we know. No game mechanics.

title: Cold War Crisis Room
subject: social-studies
concept: Advise leaders through the Cuban Missile Crisis day by day using their real options, then replay the thirteen days from Moscow and Havana to see how each side's history shaped its choices.

title: Independence Timeline
subject: social-studies
concept: Place eight independence stories from India to Mozambique on one timeline and map, tag how each was won (talks, nonviolence, armed struggle), and compare what changed and what stayed after independence.

title: Where's My Phone From?
subject: social-studies
concept: Break a phone into its parts and follow each to where it is mined, made and assembled using real trade and mineral data; investigate migration, conflict over minerals and who earns what along the chain.

title: Baron or Builder?
subject: social-studies
concept: Place five industrialists on a line from robber baron to captain of industry with evidence cards, then hear from workers, immigrants and rivals their businesses touched, and defend or move each placement.

title: Muckraker Studio
subject: social-studies
concept: Investigate a Progressive Era problem from real notes and photographs, write an expose in a 1906 magazine layout, then see which reforms followed and how the real muckrakers' reputations changed.

title: Empire Debate
subject: social-studies
concept: Argue the 1899 Senate fight over annexing the Philippines from real primary sources, then hear the Filipino voices that chamber left out and build a closing argument about the decision and its effects.

title: Stock Market 1929
subject: social-studies
concept: Trade stocks on margin in 1929; experience the crash and the New Deal response.

title: Home Front Mobilizer
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a West Coast city's war production from 1942 to 1945, then open what the official record left out: Japanese American incarceration, Black workers shut out until protest, women laid off at war's end.

title: Movement Strategy Room
subject: social-studies
concept: Plan three real campaigns (the Montgomery bus boycott, the Delano grape boycott, the 504 disability sit-in): choose tactics before seeing the organizers' choices, then judge what worked and whose roles history now recognizes.

title: Two Space Races
subject: social-studies
concept: Place the space race from Sputnik to Apollo 11 on two timelines written by Soviet and American sources; find where they disagree, what each hid or left out, and how historians later filled the gaps.

title: Decades Explorer
subject: social-studies
concept: Walk four decade rooms from the 1980s to the 2010s, pairing how each saw itself at the time with how it is remembered now, while charts track what changed and what stayed the same.

title: Build a Government
subject: social-studies
concept: Write the constitution for a newly independent country with three regions, two languages and a river shared with a neighbor; test it against crises from a contested election to a water treaty, and see which real nation's results yours resembles.

title: Who Has the Power?
subject: social-studies
concept: Sort real powers into federal, state, local, tribal, shared or international bins, replay the ones whose line moved over time, and decide where today's contested powers belong.

title: Checks and Balances
subject: social-studies
concept: Play one branch against the other two in a card game of real checks (veto, override, judicial review, confirmation), then score each route to a decision on speed, durability and rights, and replay it another way.

title: Supreme Court Simulator
subject: social-studies
concept: Hear five landmark cases brought by ordinary people, from Brown to a cheerleader's snap, argue both sides, rule as a justice, then compare your reasoning with the real majority and dissent.

title: Campaign Manager
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a fictional presidential campaign through ads, polls and the Electoral College, then replay it under a popular vote, ranked-choice and compulsory voting to see which citizens each system makes matter.

title: Who Decides?
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick a local problem (a dangerous crosswalk, a closed library branch) and trace who actually decides it: which office, which meeting, when public comment opens; then draft the testimony or petition that reaches them.

title: One More Hour
subject: social-studies
concept: Spend a Saturday one hour at a time and watch the benefit of each extra hour fall as its cost rises, then use the same marginal reasoning to argue a town policy that changes incentives for different groups.

title: Concert Ticket Market
subject: social-studies
concept: Set ticket prices; see supply and demand curves, shortages and scalpers emerge.

title: The Buyout
subject: social-studies
concept: The same phone-charger market runs twice, once with four competing makers and once after one buys out the rest; compare prices, choice and quality side by side, then see what regulators can do.

title: Economy Dashboard
subject: social-studies
concept: Read the real US economy since 1948 on one dashboard, find the recessions yourself before the official dates appear, explain what moved each indicator, then forecast the next year from leading indicators.

title: Fed Chair
subject: social-studies
concept: Chair the Fed in four real moments from 1979 to 2022, set interest rates as Congress picks fiscal policy, watch inflation and jobs respond with real lags, then compare your path with history.

title: Two Villages
subject: social-studies
concept: Farm in one of two villages, one with registered land titles and fair courts and one without, decide whether to plant an orchard, lend or start a shop, and see why secure rights and contracts change what people dare to build.

title: Trade Island
subject: social-studies
concept: Run one of two islands, find that specializing and trading leaves both better off even when one is better at everything, then add a tariff, a currency swing and a factory move and see who wins and loses.

title: Brain Explorer
subject: social-studies
concept: Turn and slice an illustrated brain, open each region through a real case like Phineas Gage, then zoom to a single neuron firing and see what drugs do at the synapse.

title: Illusion Lab
subject: social-studies
concept: Run yourself through classic illusion and memory experiments, see your own results next to typical ones, and learn how the senses and memory build, and sometimes invent, what we experience.

title: Train Your Dog
subject: social-studies
concept: Train a virtual shelter dog with classical and operant conditioning and four reinforcement schedules, watch its learning curves change, and connect each lesson to how people learn.

title: One Life, Many Stages
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow one person from infancy to old age through real developmental research (attachment, Piaget's stages, adolescence, aging), predicting each stage before the research shows it.

title: Go Along?
subject: social-studies
concept: Sit in a recreated line-judging study as classmates all answer wrong, then examine the bystander and obedience studies, what they really found and how ethical they were.

title: Trait Lab
subject: social-studies
concept: Compare trait theories of personality, ideas of intelligence and theories of motivation with the real measures behind them, take sample items, and find what each measure can and cannot tell you.

title: Case Conference
subject: social-studies
concept: Sit on a clinic team with fictional case summaries: look at each through the biological, psychological and social lenses, see how disorders are classified, compare treatments by their research evidence, and trace how stress affects health; support resources stay on every screen.

title: Wonder Kite
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick a big question you care about (Why does our town have a library?) and tie small questions to the kite's tail as map, clock, rule or coin bows; each bow that helps holds a fact and lifts the kite.

title: How Do You Know?
subject: social-studies
concept: Help a talking backpack answer "What do pandas eat?" by choosing between a zoo fact page and a toy poster, calling each line fact or opinion, and asking "How do you know?" until you know which to trust.

title: Teddy Bear Makers
subject: social-studies
concept: Put the steps of making a teddy bear in order, give each step its tool or machine and the worker with the right skill, and add up what one bear costs; then ask the bear maker questions and answer a visitor's.

title: Storm Helpers
subject: social-studies
concept: After a big storm the class walks a street to see who is affected and how (no power, a flooded road, a closed school), meets the people already helping, then picks a way kids can help and makes a poster about it.

title: Pen Pal Parcels
subject: social-studies
concept: Parcels arrive from pen pals in Ghana, Chile and Japan, each with something made there that we buy and a letter on why they trade and how their place is changing; send back something made here and pin both ways on the globe.

title: Capsule From 1965
subject: social-studies
concept: Open a time capsule a class buried under the school in 1965 (a photo, a letter, a lunch ticket, a toy catalog page); find who made each, when and where, ask your own questions, and compare those kids' wishes with yours.

title: The Last Carousel Ride
subject: social-studies
concept: The town carousel stopped running in 1975; a rider and the owner's grandson remember why in different ways, and an old newspaper adds a clue. The class compares the tellings, lists possible reasons and picks the most likely.

title: Inquiry Ladder
subject: social-studies
concept: A big question about the past (Was the railroad good for our town?) sits at the top; students climb by adding supporting questions drawn from old photos, timetables and letters, mark words people disagree about, and see each rung help.

title: Source Scout
subject: social-studies
concept: For the question Should recess be longer?, scouts choose which sources to gather (a doctor's article, a survey, a toy ad, the principal's letter), weigh who might disagree, then sort each source's lines into fact and opinion to rate its trust.

title: Made for Whom?
subject: social-studies
concept: Three sources from the state's past open one at a time (a settler's diary, a railroad poster selling land, a newspaper editorial); students infer each one's audience and purpose, spot how the maker's view shaped it, and rank which helps most.

title: Why the Pony Express Ended
subject: social-studies
concept: Evidence cards from a rider's letter, a telegraph company notice, a cost ledger and a newspaper ask why the Pony Express closed after only 18 months; students build a claim, back it with evidence from two or more sources, and defend it.

title: History Article Review
subject: social-studies
concept: Students read short kid-magazine articles about the Revolution, write each one's main claim in a sentence, then check its argument and explanation (enough evidence? steps in order? voices missing?) and give a reviewer's rating with reasons.

title: School Fix-It Meeting
subject: social-studies
concept: The class picks a school problem (a long lunch line, a crowded hallway), surveys classmates and adults on why it matters to them, talks proposals through with turn-taking rules, and votes on a plan to bring to the principal.

title: Tools for Change
subject: social-studies
concept: Cards show ways people have changed things, from petitions and boycotts to letters and voting, each with a real past and present example; students pick strategies for a local problem, predict results, and turn the plan into a letter or poster.

title: Pool Repair Vote
subject: social-studies
concept: The town pool needs repairs; students hear a grandparent, a swim team parent, a shop owner and a teen lifeguard, follow the plan from problem to hearing to vote, and choose how to pay for it: taxes, entry fees or both.

title: Ripple Street
subject: social-studies
concept: Make one kid's Saturday choices on Ripple Street (rake leaves for pay or go to the park, plant flowers, play loud music) and see the costs and benefits to the kid, the rewards and fines that nudge each choice, and the ripples on neighbors.

title: Barter Bay
subject: social-studies
concept: Fishers, bakers and potters on Barter Bay trade by swapping until shells become money and trading speeds up; then the class adds too many shells, too few, or closes the cannery to see inflation, deflation and unemployment.

title: Learn and Earn
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a kid's bike repair business for a year: spend weeks learning new skills or buying better tools, and watch how many bikes you fix and what you earn compared with a friend who never trains.

title: Interest Seesaw
subject: social-studies
concept: Put birthday money in a bank, a credit union or a savings bond and watch interest add up, then borrow for a bike and watch interest add on; a seesaw shows when interest works for you and when it works against you.

title: Skateboard Fund Chances
subject: social-studies
concept: Save toward a skateboard with chance cards each month: keep money in a jar or buy shares in the class juice company that may grow or shrink; then lock, insure or risk the skateboard as rain, a cracked wheel and a theft come up.

title: Cocoa Chain
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow cocoa from a farm in Ghana through a port and a factory to a chocolate bar here; when drought hits the farms, students explain step by step, with prices and numbers, who is affected in each country and why.

title: Panel of Experts
subject: social-studies
concept: One big question (Was the Black Death a turning point?) goes to a radio panel: a historian, an economist, a geographer and a political scientist. Students mark where the experts agree, each field's key ideas, and the smaller questions each would ask.

title: Historians Disagree
subject: social-studies
concept: Two short secondary accounts explain why the Mongol Empire grew so fast; students name each central argument, sort the kinds of sources each relied on (chronicles, letters, archaeology), and judge which argument holds up better.

title: Evidence Corkboard
subject: social-studies
concept: Pin evidence from letters, maps and toll records to answer why the Erie Canal changed New York; students string each pin to the claim, tag what each piece cannot show, and list the sources they would look for next.

title: Unlabeled Archive
subject: social-studies
concept: An archive box holds a map fragment, a letter, a coin and a woodcut with no labels; students use dated reference sources to work out who made each, when, where and for whom, then decide which help answer the archivist's question.

title: Who Gets to Vote?
subject: social-studies
concept: Dated voices from 1789 to 1870 argue about who should vote: property owners, all white men, women, free Black men. Students place each on a timeline, trace how and why views shifted, and notice whose voices were left out.

title: Museum Label Writer
subject: social-studies
concept: Write the label for a Mesopotamian clay tablet that explains how writing began, in order and with details; fix sample labels that jump around, then rewrite yours for a kids' trail card, an audio guide and the museum website.

title: Levers of Power
subject: social-studies
concept: A dangerous crossing near school is also a state road problem and a worldwide traffic safety issue; students try levers (petition, testify, vote, write the paper, organize) through the roles citizens play and judge what each can change.

title: Motion on the Floor
subject: social-studies
concept: Chair a student club meeting with an agenda, motions, an amendment and a fair vote, making sure the minority is heard, then compare how a city council, a school board and a state legislature make the same kind of choice.

title: Shaping Our Week
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow a family through one week and tap each group that shapes it: the city council's bus routes, the company where a parent works, that parent's union, the food bank, the youth soccer league; remove one and see what changes.

title: Smoke and Honey
subject: social-studies
concept: A paper mill sells cheap paper while its smoke sends neighbors to the clinic, and a beekeeper's hives help nearby orchards for free; students try a tax, a filter rule or a subsidy and watch families, the business and the town.

title: Border Trade Post
subject: social-studies
concept: Two neighboring countries swap goods at a border post: first by barter, then with money, then under a tariff on imported bikes; students tally time lost, trades made and who gains or pays: shoppers, bike makers, workers and the other country.

title: The Shrinking Lake
subject: social-studies
concept: Slide through sixty years of Lake Chad as it shrinks with drought and irrigation and the population around it grows: herders, farmers and fishers move, land use changes, and four countries choose whether to fight over it or share it.

title: Missing Voices Archive
subject: social-studies
concept: Open a real city's 1918 flu archive, full of officials' notices but missing nurses, immigrant families and Black neighborhoods; map whose voices are absent, ask questions that lead to sources filling some gaps, and watch the story change.

title: Behind the Podcast
subject: social-studies
concept: Play an original history podcast on the Great Depression, trace each claim to its cited source, flag sources that don't fit, then weigh the episode's argument against a historian's article for accuracy.

title: Claim Repair Shop
subject: social-studies
concept: Broken explanations of why the Berlin Wall fell arrive in a repair shop: contradictory evidence, steps out of order, claims too vague; diagnose each fault against real sources and rebuild a stronger claim.

title: Causes Web
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick a problem that is local and global at once (high rents, plastic waste) and build a web of causes from economics, geography, civics and history cards, then test whether the explanation holds up as a timeline, a chain or a loop.

title: Jury Room
subject: social-studies
concept: Take a seat on a twelve-person civil jury, deliberate with jurors who bring evidence and bias, reach a verdict, then run the same dispute through a town hall and a consensus circle and compare.

title: Layers and Scales
subject: social-studies
concept: Make thematic maps from real data (languages, rainfall, income) at world, country and county scale, change the class breaks and watch patterns appear or vanish, then pair the map with satellite images and photos to explain a place's politics and economy.

title: Suburb Boom
subject: social-studies
concept: Watch a metro area grow from 1945 to today on aerial images as highways, home loans and zoning rules arrive and decide who can buy where; farms become subdivisions, wetlands are paved and later flood, and students change one decision to see the pattern shift.

title: Climate on the Move
subject: social-studies
concept: Four cases on a timeline (the Little Ice Age, the Dust Bowl, Sahel droughts and a recent hurricane) show how long-term climate change and sudden disasters move people, shift farming and trade, and reshape politics far away.
